Perhaps the most beloved and certainly the one person most
associated with the Philadelphia Folk Festival from its inception,
until his death in 2020 at the age of 85, was the legendary radio
personality Gene Shay, the father of Philadelphia Folk Music.
A member of the Philadelphia Music Hall of Fame, Gene represented
all that was good about folk music both on his weekly radio show and
as emcee at nearly every Philadelphia Folk Festival evening concert
for more than 50 years. Having a distinguished advertising career, his
But he will always be remembered for his stage persona as a purveyor
of corny jokes and more importantly for the hundreds of musicians he
befriended and helped early in their careers, musicians such as Joni
Mitchell, Jim Croce, Tom Rush and so many others.

The unsung heroes in our PFF team are The Trash Committee. They work hard every day for over a week. It starts with Pre-fest Wednesday and Thursday with setting
up and clearing away the new trash. Friday, Saturday, and Sunday they exchange full trash and recycling bags for new ones throughout the campgrounds, while
cleaning up loose trash along the way. They clean up the concert areas each morning as well as a quick bag exchange on the concert hill and at the food vendors
in the evenings. Then at the end, they stay until Wednesday and clean up the entire grounds, including the parking lots and nearby roads—restoring the land to its
original beauty, leaving nothing but footprints behind. So don’t forget to clean up when you can, and show some love to our Trash Committee team members.
